_: One document style for every skill that writes a document people read: /gdoc (Google Docs, via the Docs API) and /word-doc (.docx via pandoc). Common sections apply to both. The 'gdoc' section is the owner's Google Docs look (read off their Style Guide tab 2026-09-28, block rules from their ask of 2026-09-29); /word-doc renders it too, by default since the owner kept it on 2026-09-29. The 'docx' section is the 2026-09-01 ruling (Harbor), still available with --look harbor. Colours written '@tone' resolve against the look's colour family, '@gray.tone' against the gray row, so switching 'family' keeps every role at the same relative shade.

google_palette._: The Google Docs colour picker. Each family lists its tones lightest first; a role names a tone, never a hex, so the family can change underneath it.

blocks._: Every block a skill may emit, so a Style Guide can show each one. Markdown source shape on the right.
blocks.heading: # .. ####  (title, subtitle, H1 to H6 in the ramp)
blocks.checklist: - [ ] item  (Google checkbox bullets; a ballot box in Word)
blocks.table: | a | b |  with a header row; an empty header row makes a header-less card table
blocks.table_light: <!-- table: light --> on the line before a table: the light variant
blocks.code: ``` fenced, tagged with a language (syntax coloured, markdown included)
blocks.diagram: ``` fenced, untagged: kept verbatim in monospace, 78 columns max
blocks.quote: > text  (a keyline quote with a faded opening mark)
blocks.image: ![alt](https://...png|jpg|gif)  (Google Docs fetches the URL once; local files and SVG are not inserted)
blocks.person: [Name](mailto:someone@example.com)  (a person chip in Google Docs, a mail link in Word)
blocks.date: [Oct 1, 2026](date:2026-10-01)  (a date chip in Google Docs, plain text in Word)
blocks.richlink: <https://docs.google.com/...>  a bare Google Drive, Docs, Sheets or Slides link becomes a rich link chip

table._: Filled header whose dashed border is the header colour; dashed body grid two tones lighter; body text the darkest tone; first column optionally in the lightest tone. Columns sized to content.

table_light._: The light variant for lighter concerns: no fill and no vertical lines, a dashed rule in the header colour under the header, dashed separators two tones lighter between rows. Fonts and colours from the main table.

code._: One box per block with room on all four sides and a bar on the left. Diagrams share the box without the bar; their strokes and arrowheads are drawn lighter so the labels carry the weight.

callout._: Two lines in one box: the key (glyph + LABEL, mono extra bold 8) then the text (mono 9) under it, both starting at the same indent, with air above the key and below the text.

quote._: A keyline quote on the lightest tint, with a serif opening mark in the bar's colour at the start.

docx._look: Which look /word-doc renders by default. 'gdoc' (the section above) since the owner kept it on 2026-09-29; 'harbor' (this section, the 2026-09-01 ruling) stays available with --look harbor.

palette._: Harbor, ruled on decision page doc-style-4 (D2f)

structures.table: dotted-separators: no header fill, accent header text, dashed accent rule under the header, dashed light row separators
structures.code: dotted frame + solid accent left bar over the soft-card background, applied to both code and diagram blocks
structures.toc: indent rail: accent rail on the left, level-1 entries semibold, deeper levels indented
structures.callout: type line first (glyph + label in the kind color), body below, tight gap, shared tint and bar
structures.links: accent color, no underline, anywhere including the contents list
structures.page: half-inch margins all round (halved by owner ruling 2026-09-01), footer with title left and page N of M right
structures.spacing: opened rhythm, same ruling: air after title and subtitle, around headings, between contents rows and off the rail, before and after callouts, after tables, around code and tree boxes; callouts run margin to margin with the bar in the gutter
